rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly with no reported regressions, so this round pushes obfuscation strength up while keeping cost dimensions engaged. The profile is a tiny (909 bytes text, 4 functions) numeric-kernel bundle (fannkuch, n-body, spectral-norm, partialsums) dominated by tight compute loops, so FLA gets the highest SecurityGain (0.8) since flattening is the strongest structural defense, paired with a moderate RuntimeCost (0.5) and CorrectnessRisk (0.3) to keep it off the hottest inner-loop-dominated regions if the selector deems them too costly; BCF and IBR get high SecurityGain (0.7) with mid-range cost weights so they add layered control-flow misdirection without stacking worst-case overhead on the benchmark kernels. SUB and SPLIT are nearly free and low-risk, so their cost/risk weights stay low (0.1-0.3) letting them apply broadly — SPLIT also enlarges basic-block structure that FLA/BCF/IBR can then scramble, boosting composite DiversityGain (0.7). ICALL keeps the highest CorrectnessRisk weight (0.5) because this program is mostly direct numeric code with few indirect-call sites and a hand-written-style _start, so call indirection buys little and is the likeliest correctness hazard; IGV stays mid-range as a cheap diversity add-on. With total text at only ~909 bytes, size overhead is effectively unconstrained, so SizeCost weights are kept modest except for BCF, the most size-inflating pass.
